newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka welcomes foreign criticism of rebels.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka welcomes foreign criticism of rebels.

text.p: Sri Lanka welcomed on Saturday international condemnation of attacks by Tamil Tiger rebels, saying the world was waking up to the threat they posed.

"We are glad that the international community at last has woken up to the full magnitude of the threat posed by the LTTE to peace in Sri Lanka, and in a sense to the world through their international tentacles," a Sri Lankan foreign ministry spokesman told Reuters in Colombo.
The United States on Friday condemned a spate of attacks by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels and called on the guerrillas to stop interfering with foreign ships.
"We urge the LTTE to cease all acts of terrorism," James Foley, a deputy spokesman for the U.S. State Department, said in a statement.
The United States was particularly concerned about LTTE attacks on foreign ships in Sri Lankan waters, he said.
"It is well known that LTTE has for many years taken advantage of the liberal policies in the West," the Sri Lankan spokesman said.
An LTTE spokesman in london was not immediately available for comment.
The rebels torched an Indonesian ship off the northwest coast earlier this month and kidnapped its crew of nine.
Two Indonesian crew were released. The remaining seven, all Sri Lankans, are still held captive.
Several days later the rebels hijacked a North Korean ship ferrying food and killed one of its crew. The remaining members of the crew were released.

The LTTE are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 15th year. LTTE say the toll is higher.
Last week, Amnesty International criticised LTTE for their silence over the assassination of two Sri Lankan lawmakers.

The Tamil United Liberation Front's Arunalsalam Thangathurai and the main opposition United National Party's Mohamed Moharoof were killed this month in eastern Trincomalee province. Several others, including a four-year-old boy, died in the two attacks.
Amnesty said there was mounting evidence that the LTTE were responsible for Thangathurai's death. Police have blamed the rebels for both the killings.

The United States said it supported a negotiated political settlement in Sri Lanka and believed that the Sri Lankan government proposal for constitutional reform provided a solid base for the peaceful resolution violence.

Similar views were expressed by Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer, who said in Colombo this week that Australia lent its support to Sri Lanka's efforts to find a peaceful solution to its ethnic conflict and said it was against the use of guns to grab power.
